chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Sulaymān ibn Khālid, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who stole a theft-item and denied it stubbornly, so he was beaten, and then he produced that very item itself. Is amputation incumbent upon him?
He عليه السلام said: “Yes. But if he confesses and does not bring forth the stolen property, his hand is not cut, because he confessed under punishment.”

key_terms.اعْتَرَفَ: he confessed or admitted the act
key_terms.الْعَذَابِ: punishment or torment, here referring to coercive beating
key_terms.الْقَطْعُ: the legal amputation prescribed as hadd for theft
key_terms.سَرِقَةً: a stolen item or act of theft in the legal context
key_terms.كَابَرَ: he stubbornly denied or contested the accusation

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd of amputation apply if a thief confesses under beating or only when the stolen property is produced?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses a legal ruling concerning theft and the hadd punishment. It distinguishes between a case in which the stolen item is produced and a case in which a confession is made under coercive punishment, indicating that a coerced confession alone does not establish amputation.
